alt_names: Eleventh, Twelfth and Thirteenth Dynasties of Egypt

land.text: the Theban kingdom of Mentuhotep II from Elephantine to Abydos

predecessors.note: Same state: the Thebans of the Eleventh Dynasty become the Middle Kingdom; 'Mentuhotep II, who ascended the Theban throne in 2055 BC'.

land.text: the Heracleopolitan kingdom, conquered around 2033 BC

predecessors.note: First Intermediate Period page: 'defeat the Heracleopolitan kings around 2033 BC and unify the country'.

land.text: Memphis, the Delta and Middle Egypt up to Cusae, taken by the Hyksos of Avaris

successors.note: Fifteenth Dynasty page: the Hyksos 'expanded to occupy Memphis', which 'led to the fall of the Thirteenth Dynasty there' (undated).

land.text: the Theban region: 'The 16th Dynasty (c. 1650-1580 BC) ruled the Theban region in Upper Egypt'

successors.note: Second Intermediate Period page infobox: Thebes c. 1677-1600 BC (13th, 16th and 17th Dynasties).

land.text: the eastern Delta around Avaris, a Delta kingdom from c. 1700 BC

successors.note: A state Cliopatria lacks; the Second Intermediate Period page dates the 14th Dynasty 'c. 1700-1650 BC'. It left the Middle Kingdom in -1700, before this state's end.

capitals.name: Thebes (Waset; Luxor)
capitals.note: Page infobox: capitals 'Thebes; Itjtawy'. Thebes is the capital of Mentuhotep II and the early Eleventh Dynasty.

capitals.name: Itjtawy (Amenemhat-itj-tawy; near el-Lisht)
capitals.note: Twelfth Dynasty page: Amenemhat I 'moved its capital to a new city named Amenemhat-itj-tawy'; no year given, set at his accession. Second Intermediate Period infobox 'Itjtawy: c. 1803-1677 BC (13th Dynasty)'. Coordinates are the el-Lisht area; the site itself is not located.

capitals.name: Thebes (Waset; Luxor)
capitals.note: Second Intermediate Period page infobox: 'Thebes: c. 1677-1600 BC (13th, 16th, and 17th Dynasties)'; the 13th Dynasty moved to Thebes (undated, 'possibly' under Merneferre Ay).

rulers.name: Amenemhat I
rulers.note: Twelfth Dynasty only: the page's table of c. dates; the Eleventh Dynasty and the Thirteenth Dynasty are not listed, so the strip has gaps -2055..-1992 and -1801..-1650. Boundary years are shared.

rulers.name: Sobekneferu
rulers.title: queen regnant
rulers.note: Page: 'Sobekneferu was the last king of the twelfth dynasty'.

correction.text: the Theban kingdom of Mentuhotep II, Elephantine to Abydos, before the defeat of the Heracleopolitan kings 'around 2033 BC'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page begins the Middle Kingdom c. 2055 BC with Mentuhotep II 'on the Theban throne' and the Cliopatria row only in -2000, with the whole valley. The north is not his until the 2033 defeat (First Intermediate Period page), so the Theban strip (Upper Egypt's -2061 shape) is used for 2055-2034.

correction.text: the reunited Nile valley and Delta from Elephantine to the sea; unchanged shape, years -2033..-1945

keyframe_review.note: 93,286 km2, the Nile valley and Delta, identical to the Early Dynastic and Old Kingdom shape. Page: Mentuhotep II 'would eventually defeat the Heracleopolitan kings around 2033 BC and unify the country'. Cliopatria runs the shape to -1801; the Lower Nubia colony (Senusret I) comes 'under his rule' c. 1962-1926 BC, so the plain valley is used until -1945. No infobox area on the Middle Kingdom page.

correction.text: the valley with Lower Nubia as an Egyptian colony to the Second Cataract (Buhen), Senusret I

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria adds Lower Nubia only in -1800 (the 433,182 km2 shape reaches lat 21.4, i.e. the Semna area). The page has Senusret I push 'south into Nubia as far as the Second Cataract, building a border fort at Buhen' and incorporate 'all of Lower Nubia as an Egyptian colony', and Senusret III set the boundary at Semna. The Twelfth Dynasty page gives Senusret I's reign (c. 1962-c. 1926 BC) but no year for the campaign.

correction.text: the valley, Lower Nubia and the Sinai mining camps of Amenemhat III's reign

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe adding the Sinai (28k km2 of the Cliopatria shape): 'Mining camps in the Sinai ... were operated on a semi-permanent basis' (Amenemhat III, c. 1839-c. 1814 BC; no year).

433,182 km2 (Egypt and Sudan): the valley, Lower Nubia to Semna, Sinai and 163k km2 of Western Desert plus Eastern Desert. The page names only Lower Nubia (Senusret I and III) and the Sinai mining camps; the desert hinterland is Cliopatria's and kept unverified (confidence 1 event). The page has no infobox area. The shape is right for the Twelfth Dynasty and early Thirteenth Dynasty.

correction.text: the Middle Kingdom's shape without the eastern Delta, where a Fourteenth Dynasty 'c. 1700-1650 BC' split off at Avaris

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria keeps the 433k km2 shape unchanged to -1601; the Second Intermediate Period page has a Delta family split off 'to form the 14th Dynasty (c. 1700-1650 BC)' and the Hyksos page puts a Fourteenth Dynasty kingdom at Avaris after Sobekhotep IV's death 'around 1725 BC'. The page ends the Middle Kingdom c. 1650 BC (others at Merneferre Ay c. 1700 BC), not -1601; the 'Lower Nubia' part is kept to -1651 as the page's loss of the southern forts to Kush is undated.

region.text: the Theban kingdom from Elephantine to Abydos

ledger.note: c. 2055 BC: Mentuhotep II takes the Theban throne and the Middle Kingdom begins. 'The struggle was to be concluded by Mentuhotep II, who ascended the Theban throne in 2055 BC'; infobox 'c. 2055 BC to c. 1650 BC', capital Thebes. The page names the throne, not the land.

region.text: Siut and Middle Egypt, the border province between the Theban and Heracleopolitan kingdoms

ledger.note: c. 2055 BC: Mentuhotep II's war against Heracleopolis. The First Intermediate Period page dates no campaign of his; the start is set at his accession (Middle Kingdom page, 2055 BC). Intef III had already moved 'into Middle Egypt against the Heracleopolitan kings'.

region.text: the Heracleopolitan kingdom: the Delta and Middle Egypt south to Siut

ledger.note: c. 2033 BC: Mentuhotep II conquers the north and reunites Egypt. 'would eventually defeat the Heracleopolitan kings around 2033 BC and unify the country. This event marked the beginning of the Middle Kingdom of Egypt.'
c. 2033 BC: the Heracleopolitan war ends in the Theban victory.

c. 1991 BC: Amenemhat I founds the Twelfth Dynasty. Infobox 'established c. 1991 BC'; first ruler 'Amenemhat I (c. 1991 - c. 1962 BC)'. Page: Amenemhat I 'strengthened defenses between Egypt and Asia, building the Walls of the Ruler in the East Delta region' (Middle Kingdom page, undated).
c. 1991 BC: the capital moves from Thebes to Itjtawy. Page: Amenemhat I 'moved its capital to a new city named Amenemhat-itj-tawy'; no year given, set at his accession (c. 1991 BC).

region.text: 'all of Lower Nubia as an Egyptian colony', south to the Second Cataract with the border fort at Buhen

ledger.note: c. 1944 BC: Senusret I pushes the frontier to the Second Cataract and makes Lower Nubia an Egyptian colony. 'Under his rule, Egyptian armies pushed south into Nubia as far as the Second Cataract, building a border fort at Buhen.' The page gives no year: placed at the middle of his reign (c. 1962 - c. 1926 BC, Twelfth Dynasty page). Counterpart nobody: Lower Nubia had no state in Cliopatria.

region.text: the Second Cataract and the Semna gorge, the 'unconquered Nubia' beyond the Egyptian conquests

ledger.note: c. 1873 BC: Senusret III begins his Nubian campaigns. 'He used this to launch a series of brutal campaigns in Nubia in his sixth, eighth, tenth, and sixteenth years.' Reign c. 1878 - c. 1839 BC (Twelfth Dynasty page) puts year 6 at c. 1873, 8 at 1871, 10 at 1869, 16 at 1863.

region.text: Semna, 'the formal boundary between Egyptian conquests and unconquered Nubia'

ledger.note: c. 1863 BC: after his sixteenth-year campaign Senusret III fixes the frontier at Semna. Page: 'to establish the formal boundary between Egyptian conquests and unconquered Nubia at Semna'; the boundary has no year of its own, set at the last campaign year.

region.text: the Sinai, 'mining camps ... operated on a semi-permanent basis' under Amenemhat III

ledger.note: c. 1839 BC: the Sinai mining camps are run on a semi-permanent basis under Amenemhat III (c. 1839 - c. 1814 BC). The page gives no year; placed at the start of his reign. The camps are not named, so the Sinai part of Cliopatria's shape is a researcher's reading.

region.text: the Western and Eastern Desert in Cliopatria's 433,182 km2 shape

ledger.note: c. 1800 BC: the desert hinterland joins the drawn kingdom. The page is silent on the oases and deserts; the date is the year of Cliopatria's larger shape and nothing else supports it.

region.text: the eastern Delta around Avaris, where a Delta family split off 'to form the 14th Dynasty (c. 1700-1650 BC)'

ledger.note: c. 1700 BC: a Delta kingdom, the Fourteenth Dynasty, breaks away at Avaris. The Hyksos page dates Sobekhotep IV's death 'around 1725 BC', after which 'Egypt splintered'; the page's 14th Dynasty borders (Athribis to Bubastis) are undated, so the eastern Delta is the researcher's reading. The Middle Kingdom page ends the 'Middle Kingdom' proper c. 1700 BC (Merneferre Ay) or c. 1650 BC.

region.text: Memphis and the Delta and Middle Egypt up to Cusae

ledger.note: c. 1650 BC: the Hyksos take Memphis and Lower Egypt from the Thirteenth Dynasty. Fifteenth Dynasty page: the dynasty 'expanded to occupy Memphis' leading to the fall of the Thirteenth Dynasty there (the page's words, undated); the Hyksos date from 'Established 1650 BC'.

region.text: the Theban region, ruled by the 16th Dynasty from c. 1650 BC

ledger.note: c. 1650 BC: Thebes passes to the Sixteenth Dynasty. 'The 16th Dynasty (c. 1650-1580 BC) ruled the Theban region in Upper Egypt'; Thebes c. 1677-1600 BC for the 13th, 16th and 17th Dynasties. The radius is the researcher's.

region.text: Lower Nubia and the southern forts, reoccupied by Kush

ledger.note: c. 1650 BC: Lower Nubia is lost to Kush. Second Intermediate Period page: the 13th Dynasty withdrew from the southern forts and Kush reoccupied them (a paraphrase of the page, undated, Buhen and Semna not named); placed at the Middle Kingdom's end.

region.text: the Middle Kingdom's Egypt, divided between the Hyksos at Avaris, the Sixteenth Dynasty at Thebes and Kush

ledger.note: c. 1650 BC: the Middle Kingdom ends and the Second Intermediate Period begins. Infobox 'c. 2055 BC to c. 1650 BC'; 'the Middle Kingdom would end around 1650 BC' if the Thirteenth Dynasty is included; 'followed by the Second Intermediate Period of Egypt, another period of division that involved foreign rule of Lower Egypt by the Hyksos'.

wars.name: Reunification of Egypt under Mentuhotep II

zones.text: Siut and Middle Egypt, between Thebes and Heracleopolis

wars.outcome: Mentuhotep II 'would eventually defeat the Heracleopolitan kings around 2033 BC and unify the country'.
wars.note: The page dates the end (around 2033 BC) and Mentuhotep II's stela 'ca. 2051-2030'; the start is his accession in 2055 BC (Middle Kingdom page) and no battle is dated.

wars.name: Nubian campaigns of Senusret I

zones.text: Lower Nubia to the Second Cataract

wars.outcome: Lower Nubia incorporated 'as an Egyptian colony' with a border fort at Buhen.
wars.note: Span is his reign (c. 1962 - c. 1926 BC, Twelfth Dynasty page); no campaign year on either page. The Twelfth Dynasty page says instead that he 'expanded Egyptian control to the Third Cataract', which the Middle Kingdom page and Semna do not support.

wars.name: Nubian campaigns of Senusret III

zones.text: the Second Cataract and the Semna gorge

wars.outcome: Campaigns in his 6th, 8th, 10th and 16th years ended with the formal boundary at Semna between Egyptian conquests and unconquered Nubia.
wars.note: BCE years are computed from the regnal years and the Twelfth Dynasty page's reign (c. 1878 - c. 1839 BC); the page says 'revered as a god in Nubia' and 'brutal campaigns'.

wars.name: Middle Kingdom campaigns into Canaan
wars.outcome: No territorial result: Amenemhat I's armies 'campaigned ... into southern Canaan' (Twelfth Dynasty page); 'One of Senusret's soldiers records a campaign into Canaan, perhaps against Shechem' (Middle Kingdom page); Byblos kept diplomatic ties.
wars.note: Undated; the span is Amenemhat I to Senusret III. The Hyksos page calls the Sebek-khu stele under Senusret III (1878-1839 BC) 'the earliest known Egyptian campaign in the Levant'. Nothing is drawn.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines; the valley is bounded by desert. The Semna boundary with unconquered Nubia (c. 1863 BC) is a formal fortified frontier, the best-defined edge, but not a surveyed or treaty line.

notes: Cliopatria's three shapes (-2000..-1801: 93,286 km2 valley; -1800..-1701 and -1700..-1601: 433,182 km2 with Lower Nubia, Sinai and the deserts). Dates follow the pages (c. 2055 to c. 1650 BC) against Cliopatria's -2000..-1601; the dossier starts as the Theban kingdom of 2055 (the same state as upper-egypt) and takes the whole valley only from the 2033 conquest. PAGE CONFLICTS: the Middle Kingdom page begins the period with Mentuhotep II's accession in 2055 BC but the First Intermediate Period page dates the Heracleopolitan defeat to around 2033 BC; the Twelfth Dynasty page dates the dynasty c. 1991-c. 1802 BC, the Middle Kingdom page (Yurco) 1991-1786 BC, and the Turin Royal Canon 1991-1778 BC; the Twelfth Dynasty page puts Senusret I's frontier at the Third Cataract, the Middle Kingdom page at the Second; the Second Intermediate Period page gives the 13th Dynasty c. 1773-1650 BC in the text but Itjtawy c. 1803-1677 BC in its infobox. The Middle Kingdom page also says the period lasted 'from approximately 2040 to 1782 or 1700 BC (depending on the definition)'. The end -1650 includes the Thirteenth Dynasty; a stricter end is c. 1700. NOT DRAWN: the Walls of the Ruler (East Delta; undated), Byblos (diplomatic), Faiyum reclamation (Senusret II, no territory). States needed from other groups: fourteenth-dynasty-of-egypt (Avaris, c. 1700-1650), the Abydos Dynasty (c. 1640-1620), and a Kerma/Kush state of Upper Nubia (counterpart in the Nubian events). Gazetteer names needed: Itjtawy, Buhen, Semna, Kerma. The Lower Nubia and Sinai regions in the keyframes are intersected with Cliopatria's -1800 shape so they match its cells.
